hyperedges.label: Profit Ledger From Sync To Reports

nodes.label: Profit Intelligence
nodes.rationale: Shopify embedded app that calculates real profit, detects profit leakage, and recommends actions.

nodes.label: apps/web
nodes.rationale: Next.js UI. Embedded Shopify UI arrives in Phase 3.

nodes.label: apps/api
nodes.rationale: NestJS on Fastify. REST under /api/v1.

nodes.label: apps/worker
nodes.rationale: Background worker. pg-boss handlers arrive in later phases.

nodes.label: packages/config
nodes.rationale: Zod-validated environment loading.

nodes.label: packages/contracts
nodes.rationale: Shared API request and response schemas.

nodes.label: infra/docker
nodes.rationale: Local PostgreSQL via Docker Compose.

nodes.label: Phase 13 Security and Production Readiness
nodes.rationale: Implemented. Next is Phase 14, deployment and beta.

nodes.label: Table Category Prefixes
nodes.rationale: Database tables use lowercase snake_case with a category prefix (m_, s_, t_, f_, o_, a_). See prompt/prompt.md section 32.

nodes.label: Competitor Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Written 2026-10-09 against TrueProfit, BeProfit, Lifetimely by AMP, MerchantFlow, PodVector, and Triple Whale. ProfitFly was not found on the Shopify App Store so it is not compared. Competitor facts come from public listings and may be out of date.

nodes.label: Lifetimely
nodes.rationale: Cohorts, LTV, and CAC payback are Lifetimely's core.

nodes.label: MerchantFlow
nodes.rationale: Bank reconciliation for untracked expenses is a MerchantFlow idea.

nodes.label: Triple Whale
nodes.rationale: First-party pixel attribution and creative analytics are Triple Whale's core.

nodes.label: V1 Launch Scope
nodes.rationale: The smallest product merchants will pay for. The first six items decide whether the profit figure is right and whether the app can be approved and sold.

nodes.label: Meta and Google Ads Integration
nodes.rationale: Daily spend sync by campaign, blended ROAS and MER, and profit after ads. Every compared competitor has live ad spend; manual entry cannot be the product. The owner must create the Meta and Google developer apps because review takes weeks.

nodes.label: Actual Shopify Payments Fees
nodes.rationale: Balance transactions replace the estimate that currently flags every order. Gateway rules stay for PayPal and others. Needs the payments read scope and a Shopify Payments store to test.

nodes.label: Shipping Cost by Zone, Country and Weight
nodes.rationale: Most unprofitable-order warnings today come from shipping cost missing. Includes CSV import.
nodes.norm_label: shipping cost by zone, country and weight

nodes.label: Product Cost CSV and Bulk Edit
nodes.rationale: Import, export, and bulk edit by product, variant, collection, and vendor. Today costs are edited on a per-product screen.
nodes.norm_label: product cost csv and bulk edit

nodes.label: Live Billing and Plans
nodes.rationale: Choose managed pricing or the Billing API, approve prices, and switch BILLING_MODE on. Trial, upgrade, and downgrade must be tested. Prices are an owner decision.

nodes.label: App Store Readiness
nodes.rationale: Phase 14: HTTPS hosting, monitoring alerts, backups restored, privacy policy, support contact, listing text and screenshots, read_all_orders approval or a 60-day history, performance and accessibility, and rotation of the leaked Shopify secret.

nodes.label: Exchange Rates for Any Currency
nodes.rationale: A daily rates source is needed. Today only USD and AED are supported.

nodes.label: Production Email Delivery
nodes.rationale: SMTP or a mail service for scheduled reports and alerts. The code is done; the owner provides the account.

nodes.label: Email Alerts
nodes.rationale: Margin drop, loss orders, missing costs, and failed sync. Today they are in-app only.

nodes.label: read_all_orders Launch Decision
nodes.rationale: Owner must choose whether to apply for read_all_orders or limit history to 60 days at launch.

nodes.label: LTV and Cohort Privacy Boundary
nodes.rationale: Customer lifetime value, cohorts, and CAC payback need customer-level data and Shopify approval for protected customer data. That would change the privacy position because the app deliberately stores no customer personal data today.

nodes.label: Order-to-Campaign UTM Attribution
nodes.rationale: V2. Profit per campaign, not just per account. Shopify orders are not matched to campaigns yet.

nodes.label: First-party Pixel Attribution
nodes.rationale: V3. Triple Whale's core. Heavy engineering and a privacy review.

nodes.label: Shopify App Pricing
nodes.rationale: Recommendation: BILLING_MODE=managed. It is the default Shopify steers new public apps to, needs the least code, and the owner controls prices in the Partner Dashboard without a deploy. Shopify is the source of truth: the app reads currentAppInstallation.activeSubscriptions and never stores card details or prices paid.

nodes.label: Billing API
nodes.rationale: BILLING_MODE=api is implemented for pricing models managed pricing cannot express, including one-time or unusual pricing. Shopify still supports it and describes it as the older method. The app creates the subscription and sends the merchant to a confirmation URL.

nodes.label: Plan Catalogue
nodes.rationale: packages/contracts/src/plans.ts holds every plan and limit. Nothing else hard-codes a plan check. Growth and Pro prices are drafts (approved false) until the owner approves them.

nodes.label: Free Plan
nodes.rationale: 30 days of history, 5 reports a month, no PDF, no scheduled emails, 1 advertising account, no profit leakage findings, draft price $0.

nodes.label: Growth Plan
nodes.rationale: 90 days of history, 50 reports, PDF, 3 scheduled emails, 3 advertising accounts, leakage findings, draft price $29. approved is false, so it cannot be bought in Billing API mode and the screen marks it Draft.

nodes.label: Pro Plan
nodes.rationale: 90 days of history, 500 reports, PDF, 10 scheduled emails, 10 advertising accounts, leakage findings, draft price $79. approved is false. When billing is off, BILLING_OFF_PLAN defaults to pro.

nodes.label: Billing Mode Off
nodes.rationale: Default for development and beta. Every shop gets BILLING_OFF_PLAN and the history window is not limited, so nothing blocks testing. Subscribing is refused with a clear message.

nodes.label: Unrecognized Subscription Means Free
nodes.rationale: In managed or api mode a shop is on the plan of its active Shopify subscription, otherwise Free. FROZEN, CANCELLED, DECLINED, EXPIRED, PENDING, or an unrecognised plan name all mean Free, so a shop is never given more than it pays for because something did not match.

nodes.label: EntitlementsService
nodes.rationale: apps/api/src/billing. Called by every endpoint that has a limit so a direct API request gets the same answer as a click.

nodes.label: plan_limit 403
nodes.rationale: 403 plan_limit names the limit and which plan includes it. Enforced for period reach, report files per month, PDF files, scheduled emails, advertising accounts, and leakage findings. Failed report files do not count. The comparison period is held to the same window.

nodes.label: POST /billing/subscribe
nodes.rationale: Returns only a Shopify URL: Shopify's plan page in managed mode, or the confirmation URL of a subscription the app creates in api mode. Test charge outside production unless BILLING_TEST_MODE=false.

nodes.label: app_subscriptions/update Webhook
nodes.rationale: The webhook, or the Check my plan again button, makes the app re-read the subscription from Shopify and store it. The webhook payload itself is not trusted.

nodes.label: Onboarding Checklist
nodes.rationale: GET /session computes the checklist from real data: connected, order history imported, product costs, payment fees, shipping costs, and optional expenses. The card folds away when the required steps are done.

nodes.label: POST /support
nodes.rationale: Stores feedback, a question, or a problem with the shop and user from the session, never from the request. A few messages per hour per shop. The form asks not to include customer details. Messages are removed when the shop is purged.

nodes.label: Downgrade Pauses Without Deleting
nodes.rationale: Nothing is deleted when a plan gets smaller. The history window only limits what can be viewed. Scheduled emails beyond the new limit are paused, the oldest are kept, and they can be resumed after upgrading. Accounts, expenses, costs, and report files stay. Tested in billing.integration.test.ts.

nodes.label: Dashboard Overview Endpoint
nodes.rationale: GET /api/v1/dashboard/overview. Period is in the shop time zone. Presets are 7d, 14d, 30d, 60d, 90d, or custom. The previous period is the same length immediately before. Deltas are relative changes and are null when the previous value is zero. Margin change is in percentage points.

nodes.label: summarizeFromTotals
nodes.rationale: Totals come from SQL aggregates over the profit ledger and go through summarizeFromTotals so they equal the engine's entry-based summary.

nodes.label: Dashboard Alerts
nodes.rationale: Deterministic rules in apps/api/src/dashboard/alerts.ts. Each alert has evidence, why, and an optional action. Lost money is claimed only when every cost for those orders is known; otherwise it says may be losing money.

nodes.label: Overview UI
nodes.rationale: apps/web/components/overview. Period, custom dates, and currency filters. Currency choice is kept in localStorage only. KPI cards, Recharts trend with a data-table alternative, confidence and cost breakdowns, and alerts. Display formatting is in lib/format.ts.

nodes.label: Display Currency Conversion
nodes.rationale: Amounts are converted per day to the chosen display currency when a rate exists (USD/AED peg). Otherwise the response falls back to the shop currency and says why in currency.note.

nodes.label: Counted Order Statuses
nodes.rationale: Only paid, partially refunded, and refunded orders count. Unpaid orders are reported separately as awaiting payment.

nodes.label: Deferred Product Ranking
nodes.rationale: Top and least profitable products need an approved rule for allocating order-level discounts and refunds to products, so that ranking is part of Phase 8.

nodes.label: Drizzle ORM
nodes.rationale: Reviewed SQL migrations live in packages/db/migrations. Never edit an applied migration. Production migrations run with owner credentials from the deployment environment, not from a developer machine.

nodes.label: m_tenant
nodes.rationale: Merchant account and the isolation boundary. Status is active, suspended, or deleted.

nodes.label: m_shop
nodes.rationale: Shopify store installation. UNIQUE(shopify_domain) and UNIQUE(tenant_id, id), which is the target of composite foreign keys.

nodes.label: s_shop_credential
nodes.rationale: Encrypted offline access token. Composite foreign key (tenant_id, shop_id) to m_shop so a credential cannot point at another tenant's shop.

nodes.label: withTenant
nodes.rationale: Runs the callback in a transaction after set_config('app.tenant_id', id, true). The setting is transaction-local so it never leaks across pooled connections.

nodes.label: app_current_tenant
nodes.rationale: Policies use app_current_tenant(), which is NULL when unset, so no rows match. Fail closed.

nodes.label: resolveTenantByShopDomain
nodes.rationale: The only bootstrap lookup. It sets app.shop_domain and a read-only policy lets the matching m_shop row be selected. Pass only a domain already verified from a Shopify session token or webhook HMAC. Tenant ids and domains must come from server-side verified context, never from request input.

nodes.label: Forced Row Level Security
nodes.rationale: Every migration that creates a table must GRANT to app_user, enable and force RLS, and add a policy. A test fails if a table lacks forced RLS or a policy.

nodes.label: app_user
nodes.rationale: DATABASE_URL role used by the api and the worker. DML on listed tables only. Not superuser, no BYPASSRLS, cannot create objects.

nodes.label: DATABASE_ADMIN_URL
nodes.rationale: Owner and migrator role. Used by migrations and db commands only. Owns the tables.

nodes.label: f_expense_override
nodes.rationale: Replaces or skips one month of a recurring expense. Saving the same month twice replaces it.

nodes.label: expensesForPeriod
nodes.rationale: packages/profit-engine/src/expenses.ts. Occurrences are computed, never stored, so a retried request or job cannot create a duplicate charge. One-time counts in full on its date. Monthly spreads each month evenly over its days with cumulative rounding so adjacent periods add up to the whole month. Yearly counts in full on each anniversary, a cash view like refunds; 29 February falls on 28 February in a normal year.

nodes.label: Expense Amount Versioning
nodes.rationale: Changing an amount closes the old row the day before the first month it applies to and starts a new row via replaces_id, so earlier months keep the amount that applied then. The database only lets end_date and revoked_at change on an existing expense.

nodes.label: Expense requestKey
nodes.rationale: Creating is safe to retry. The same requestKey in the same shop returns the first expense instead of adding another.

nodes.label: a_audit_log
nodes.rationale: Every expense create, change, stop, removal, and month edit records who, what, and the old and new value.

nodes.label: Net Profit
nodes.rationale: Net profit on the Overview is contribution profit minus advertising and operating expenses. When no expense exists the figure is contribution only, never a net profit that silently ignores costs.

nodes.label: AdProvider
nodes.rationale: apps/worker/src/ads/sync.ts defines the AdProvider interface and a registry. Providers are added one at a time. Today only manual entry exists. Meta, Google, and TikTok show as not connected yet because each needs a developer app and credentials only the owner can create, and the screen says so instead of pretending.

nodes.label: Daily Ad Spend Sync
nodes.rationale: At 06:00 UTC the worker re-reads the last 7 days for every account whose provider has an importer. Spend is upserted by account, date, and campaign, so a second run or a revised platform number never counts spend twice. A failing account is flagged with a generic message because provider errors can echo tokens, and it does not stop the others.

nodes.label: Honest Ad Attribution
nodes.rationale: Platform-reported sales are the platform's own claim and are shown apart from Shopify sales. Shopify orders are not matched to campaigns yet, so return is shown blended (all Shopify revenue over all ad spend) and as the platform reports it.

nodes.label: Ad Spend Counted Once
nodes.rationale: Ad spend lowers contribution profit once. Overview, trend, product reconciliation, and reports all use the same figure. Products plus unallocated items, including advertising, equal the Overview figure.

nodes.label: evaluateLeakage
nodes.rationale: packages/reports/src/leakage.ts. A pure function: the same figures and limits always give the same findings, so every finding can be reproduced from the numbers on screen.

nodes.label: Leakage Finding
nodes.rationale: A finding states a measured fact (evidence), why it matters (why), where to act (action), and, only when it is defensible, the money involved (impact). Impact is always a loss and always has a note.

nodes.label: Missing Data Is Never Guessed
nodes.rationale: An order that looks negative but is missing a cost is only a possible loss with no money figure. A product without a cost is not judged, and the finding says how many were skipped.

nodes.label: Small Sample Gate
nodes.rationale: A margin or refund rate needs at least 10 orders. A product margin needs at least 3 units. Small samples are not judged.

nodes.label: Merchant Alert Limits
nodes.rationale: Limits belong to the merchant in Settings, Alerts. Every comparison is strict: exactly at the limit raises nothing.

nodes.label: loss_orders
nodes.rationale: Critical when orders with every cost known have negative profit. Money figure is the total loss of those orders.

nodes.label: possible_loss
nodes.rationale: Info when profit is negative but a cost is missing. No money figure.

nodes.label: Daily Leakage Check
nodes.rationale: At 05:00 UTC the last 30 days are checked. Warning and critical findings create a notification once per week per rule. Informational findings never interrupt. Plans without leakage findings get neither the tab nor the notifications.

nodes.label: System Monitoring
nodes.rationale: apps/worker/src/monitoring is separate from merchant findings. See docs/operations/monitoring.md.

nodes.label: Profit Engine Package
nodes.rationale: packages/profit-engine. Money, rounding, currency conversion, calculateOrder, summarize, and confidence. No database, no clock, no network. Financial rules exist only in the engine. The API, the worker, and the database never re-implement a formula.

nodes.label: f_profit_entry
nodes.rationale: The ledger: one row per component per event with date in the shop time zone, amount, status, source, basis, and engine version. Every number is a sum of these rows.

nodes.label: f_order_profit
nodes.rationale: One row per order: counted or why not, review flags, partial flag, and order business date.

nodes.label: f_product_cost
nodes.rationale: Effective-dated cost per variant. Append-only; revoke instead of edit. The unit cost used for a line is stored with its ledger entry and reused by routine recalculations. Only an explicit force recalculation applies a new cost. A cost with a later effective date never changes older orders.

nodes.label: s_payment_fee_rule
nodes.rationale: Estimate rule, effective dated, append-only.

nodes.label: s_shipping_cost_rule
nodes.rationale: Estimate rule, effective dated, append-only.

nodes.label: s_app_setting
nodes.rationale: Missing-cost warning threshold, default 10%.

nodes.label: profit.recalculate
nodes.rationale: apps/worker profit/recalculate.ts. Runs the engine over orders 100 per transaction and replaces each order's ledger. Triggered when sync finishes or an order or refund webhook arrives. Idempotent: rows are replaced, never appended, and the order row is locked first so overlapping runs cannot duplicate.

nodes.label: Missing Amount Is Not Invented
nodes.rationale: A missing cost, fee, or shipping cost is an entry with status missing and amount 0, counted in the confidence and shown as partial profit.

nodes.label: Exact Decimal Money
nodes.rationale: decimal.js, stored as NUMERIC(19,4), rounded once per entry to the currency minor unit, half away from zero.

nodes.label: Measure First
nodes.rationale: There is no daily summary table yet because sums over the indexed ledger are cheap. A summary table will be added when a measurement shows it is needed. Spec section 11.

nodes.label: Append-only Costs, Rules, and Audit
nodes.rationale: The application role has UPDATE only on the revoked columns of cost and rule tables and no UPDATE on the audit log. a_audit_log is never updated.

nodes.label: pnpm profit:verify
nodes.rationale: Against the dev store, revenue plus tax equals Shopify's order total on every counted order, every refund reconciles to the money returned, and the approved examples reproduce to the cent.

nodes.label: Product Profitability Endpoints
nodes.rationale: GET /api/v1/profitability/products and products/detail. Tenant-scoped, session required. Periods use the same presets and rules as the Overview. Amounts are in the shop currency.

nodes.label: Order Profitability Endpoints
nodes.rationale: GET /api/v1/profitability/orders and orders/:id. One order returns every ledger entry with a plain-language explanation, a per-product split, and unallocated items.

nodes.label: Approved Allocation Rule
nodes.rationale: Sales and discounts are split in proportion to each line's value before discount. A refund goes to the lines that were refunded. Product cost is already per line. Shipping charged, shipping refunded, payment fees, and shipping cost stay with the order and are shown as unallocated. Splitting uses whole minor units and largest remainder so the parts always add up exactly.

nodes.label: packages/profit-engine/src/allocate.ts
nodes.rationale: Pure and unit tested.

nodes.label: Contribution Profit Reconciliation
nodes.rationale: For a period, sum of product profit plus unallocated equals dashboard contribution profit, to the cent. Order profits also add up to the dashboard figure. Only entries dated inside the period are allocated, so refunds land in the period of the refund, a cash view, as on the Overview.

nodes.label: Ledger Explainability
nodes.rationale: Each ledger entry returns a label, its data quality (confirmed, estimated, or missing), its source, and a sentence saying how it was worked out. A missing cost is described as unknown, never as zero.

nodes.label: Allocate in Application Code
nodes.rationale: Product figures are allocated in application code per request because exact cent-level splitting is awkward in SQL. This is fine for typical periods; measure before adding a summary table. Order lists are paged in SQL.

nodes.label: @pi/reports
nodes.rationale: The package builds reports. The API shows them and the worker prepares files. Both use the same code, so the screen, the CSV, and the PDF always show the same figures.

nodes.label: Report Builders
nodes.rationale: packages/reports/src/builders.ts. profit_loss, products, orders, marketing, and expenses. A report is a plain table of strings: money as exact decimals, formatted only for reading.

nodes.label: Profit and Loss Report
nodes.rationale: One column per calendar month plus a total. Within a month, revenue less costs gives contribution profit, and less advertising and expenses gives net profit. Tested to the cent against the Overview.

nodes.label: o_report_export
nodes.rationale: POST /api/v1/reports/exports queues a background job. The worker builds CSV or A4 landscape PDF, stores up to 20 MB, and keeps it 7 days. Only the worker that moves the export from queued to running does the work. Failures are stored, a critical notification is created, and the merchant can retry. At most 5 exports waiting or running per shop.

nodes.label: CSV Formula Guard
nodes.rationale: Text cells that start with =, +, -, or @ get a leading apostrophe so a product or order name cannot run as a spreadsheet formula. Numbers are never altered. UTF-8 with a byte order mark so Excel reads it. Download needs the session token and nosniff, no-store, attachment headers.

nodes.label: s_report_schedule
nodes.rationale: Weekly on a weekday or monthly on the 1st, at an hour, in the shop time zone, up to 5 recipients and 10 schedules.

nodes.label: latestOccurrence
nodes.rationale: packages/reports/src/schedule.ts. Answers when the schedule last fired and which period it covers from the clock alone, so a worker that was down at the scheduled hour catches up, and the answer is the same however often it is asked.

nodes.label: Schedule Period Claim
nodes.rationale: The period end is claimed in one UPDATE WHERE last_period_end is older, before anything is queued, so overlapping schedulers or a restart cannot send a period twice. A new schedule starts with the next firing and does not send the period that has just passed. One delivery row exists per export and recipient.

nodes.label: SMTP Email
nodes.rationale: Uses SMTP_URL and MAIL_FROM. Without it every delivery is marked failed with a clear message and can be retried once mail is set up. Each recipient succeeds or fails on its own.

nodes.label: o_notification
nodes.rationale: Shown on the Reports screen and as a one-line reminder on the Overview. A dedupe_key stops the same event creating two messages.

nodes.label: Seven-day Export Retention
nodes.rationale: Export files are deleted after 7 days by the nightly cleanup deleteExpiredExports. Purging a shop removes its exports, schedules, deliveries, and notifications.

nodes.label: Variant Cost Settings
nodes.rationale: GET and PUT /api/v1/settings/costs. A cost for the same date replaces the earlier one, which stays in history. Dates cannot be in the future or before 2000.

nodes.label: Fee and Shipping Rules
nodes.rationale: Payment fee rules are percent plus fixed, per gateway or all. Shipping cost rules are flat or a percent of shipping charged. The missing-cost warning limit is also set here.

nodes.label: fill_gaps Recalculation
nodes.rationale: Saving a cost or rule does not change past orders by itself. Apply to existing orders prices orders whose cost was missing and applies fee and shipping rules. Costs already used on past orders stay.

nodes.label: everything Recalculation
nodes.rationale: Recalculate everything also redoes costs already used, can change figures already seen, needs a second confirmation in the UI, and is written to the audit trail.

nodes.label: Shop Taken From Session
nodes.rationale: The shop is always taken from the session token. No shop or tenant id is accepted from the client. A cost, rule, or audit row of another shop is never readable or removable (404). Every change records the Shopify user id from the session token.

nodes.label: Gift Cards Cannot Have a Cost
nodes.norm_label: gift cards cannot have a cost

nodes.label: packages/db/src/profit.ts
nodes.rationale: Writes costs and rules and the audit trail.

nodes.label: Managed Installation
nodes.rationale: Scopes come from shopify.app.toml. There is no OAuth redirect code.

nodes.label: App Bridge ID Token
nodes.rationale: JWT, HS256, signed with the app secret, about 60 seconds. The page calls /api/v1 on its own origin with Authorization Bearer. Next.js rewrites /api/v1 to the api, so the api is never public on its own.

nodes.label: SessionGuard
nodes.rationale: Verifies signature, expiry, aud equal to SHOPIFY_API_KEY, and that dest and iss name the same myshopify.com host. No tenant or shop id is ever read from the request.

nodes.label: Offline Token Exchange
nodes.rationale: Non-expiring offline access token (expiring=false) chosen to avoid refresh concurrency. Revisit if Shopify requires expiring tokens for App Store review.

nodes.label: installShop
nodes.rationale: Unknown or returning uninstalled shop: token exchange, shop name, currency, and time zone query, then an idempotent install that creates tenant, shop, and credential in one transaction. Concurrent first requests are safe because of the unique constraint; the loser re-reads. A known active shop makes no call to Shopify.

nodes.label: AES-256-GCM Token Encryption
nodes.rationale: TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY. Access tokens are encrypted before storage, with a key id stored per row for rotation, and are never returned by any endpoint. The API key is public. The API secret and encryption key live only in .env or deployment secrets.

nodes.label: AuthError
nodes.rationale: @shopify/shopify-api puts the raw token into its error messages, so the wrapper discards library errors and throws a generic AuthError. Do not log library error text.

nodes.label: Next.js Client Plus Separate API
nodes.rationale: Option 1 is confirmed viable. No fallback to the React Router template is needed. The api must be started separately. shopify.web.toml works, but the web dev script must read PORT because the CLI assigns a random port.

nodes.label: frame-ancestors
nodes.rationale: Allows https://*.myshopify.com and https://admin.shopify.com. Per-shop restriction can be added later.

nodes.label: Webhook Subscriptions Phase 5
nodes.rationale: Webhooks use HMAC of the raw body. Subscriptions and compliance topics are Phase 5.

nodes.label: o_sync_job
nodes.rationale: One active job per shop, enforced by a unique index. Status moves from queued to succeeded, partial, or failed.

nodes.label: sync.shop Queue
nodes.rationale: pg-boss queue. Policy exclusive, singletonKey is the shop id. The api enqueues after createSyncJob.

nodes.label: runSync
nodes.rationale: Products, then orders whose processed_at is within the last 90 days. One transaction per page upserts rows and saves the resume cursor and progress counters. One page of 25 orders is in memory at a time.

nodes.label: Synced Shopify Tables
nodes.rationale: t_product, t_product_variant, t_order, t_order_line_item, t_refund, t_refund_line_item, t_order_transaction, and o_sync_job. All carry tenant_id and shop_id, a composite foreign key to m_shop, forced RLS, and UNIQUE(shop_id, shopify_id). No customer personal data is stored. Money is NUMERIC(19,4) in shop currency.

nodes.label: Sync Page Idempotency
nodes.rationale: INSERT ON CONFLICT (shop_id, shopify_id) DO UPDATE. Replaying a page changes nothing. Duplicates inside one batch are collapsed and the newest wins.

nodes.label: No Rollback to Older Shopify Data
nodes.rationale: Update only where the incoming shopify_updated_at is at least the stored value. A stale order is skipped together with its children. Line items missing from a new copy are deleted unless Shopify said the list was truncated.
nodes.norm_label: no rollback to older shopify data

nodes.label: Resumable Sync
nodes.rationale: Cursor and counters are written in the same transaction as each page. A retry restarts at the last committed page. pg-boss returns jobs of crashed workers after expireInSeconds. Five retries with a 30 second base and exponential backoff. 401 or 403 is not retried: the job fails and the shop is flagged reauth_required.

nodes.label: Cost-aware Shopify Client
nodes.rationale: Sleeps using throttleStatus before the bucket empties, and retries THROTTLED, 429 using Retry-After, and 5xx with backoff.

nodes.label: Paginated GraphQL
nodes.rationale: Chosen instead of bulk operations for now. Seeded history is 150 orders; paging 25 orders per request streams in constant memory and is resumable. For stores with tens of thousands of orders, add a bulk-operation source behind the same runSync stages. Nested refund line items need care in bulk JSONL.

nodes.label: Refund Effective Date
nodes.rationale: The profit engine must use t_refund.processed_at. The REFUND transaction timestamp is the creation time and can be months later. Cancelling an unpaid order creates a refund with line items but 0.00 money and must not count as a monetary refund.

nodes.label: NULL Means Unknown
nodes.rationale: fee_amount NULL means Shopify reports no fee data, never zero. t_product_variant.unit_cost_amount NULL means no cost is set. Orders keep processed_at as the business date; shopify_created_at is only the import time for backdated orders.

nodes.label: Use Shopify Discount Amounts
nodes.rationale: Shopify rounds percentage discounts slightly differently from a per-line calculation. Always use the amounts Shopify reports; never recompute discounts. t_order.subtotal_amount is after discounts and before shipping.

nodes.label: read_all_orders History Limit
nodes.rationale: Orders older than 60 days need the read_all_orders scope for real merchants. Seeded orders have createdAt equal to now, so the dev store does not exercise that limit.

nodes.label: Webhooks and Privacy Handling
nodes.rationale: Live updates, the nightly reconcile, and uninstall and privacy handling are described in webhooks.md. A re-sync re-imports the 90 day window idempotently.

nodes.label: HMAC-SHA256 Webhook Verification
nodes.rationale: Nothing else is trusted first. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over the exact raw body with a constant-time compare, so a forged, tampered, or unsigned request is 401 and is not stored.

nodes.label: o_webhook_event
nodes.rationale: Unique on shop_id plus X-Shopify-Webhook-Id so a Shopify redelivery is a duplicate acknowledgement. Concurrent duplicates yield one row and one job. Rows store topic, ids, and status, never payloads.

nodes.label: webhook.process Job
nodes.rationale: The API enqueues the job and answers 200 within milliseconds. If enqueue fails, the event row is removed and the API returns 500 so Shopify's retry is treated as new work.

nodes.label: processWebhook
nodes.rationale: The handler never trusts the webhook payload. It re-reads the resource from Shopify and upserts only data that is new or newer, so out-of-order delivery stays correct.

nodes.label: Nightly Reconcile
nodes.rationale: Delivery is at-least-once and not ordered, so correctness cannot depend on payloads. At 03:00 UTC the job asks what changed since the last good sync minus one day; Sundays re-check the full 90-day window. It cannot yet detect an order deleted in Shopify while its webhook was missed.

nodes.label: app/uninstalled
nodes.rationale: The token is removed, running syncs are cancelled, the shop is marked uninstalled, and a purge is scheduled in 30 days.

nodes.label: shop/redact
nodes.rationale: Mandatory privacy topic. All data of the shop is deleted immediately, overriding the uninstall grace period.

nodes.label: Customer Privacy Webhook Acknowledgement
nodes.rationale: customers/redact and customers/data_request are acknowledged with no export or erasure because no customer personal data is stored.

nodes.label: Webhook IDs Only
nodes.rationale: Order, refund, and product subscriptions request include_fields ids only so customer data is never delivered to the app.

nodes.label: 90-Day Order History Window
nodes.rationale: Only orders inside the 90-day window are stored. A webhook for an older order that is not held is ignored, but an order already held is still updated so late refunds are applied.

nodes.label: Webhook Event Retention
nodes.rationale: Event rows without payloads are deleted after 14 days by a nightly cleanup at 03:30 UTC.

nodes.label: pg-boss Webhook Retries
nodes.rationale: Failed processing is retried 8 times with backoff. Permanent failure is recorded on the event. A revoked token stops retries and flags the shop for reconnection.

nodes.label: Next.js Embedded Client
nodes.rationale: Next.js stays the embedded client and calls a separate API. A Phase 3 spike must prove install, token exchange, and an authenticated call. The official React Router template is a fallback only with explicit approval.

nodes.label: NestJS on Fastify
nodes.rationale: NestJS on the Fastify adapter is the structured backend. Current Nest releases are ESM-only, so the API, worker, and packages use type module and nodenext. TypeScript is pinned to 6.0.x because typescript-eslint does not yet support 7.x. The Phase 1 worker is a plain Node process until job handlers need shared services.

nodes.label: Drizzle ORM
nodes.rationale: Drizzle is paired with reviewed SQL migrations so schema changes stay explicit rather than hidden behind a generated client.

nodes.label: pg-boss Queue
nodes.rationale: pg-boss runs on PostgreSQL. Redis is excluded from V1 so the solo-developer stack does not add another operational service.

nodes.label: pnpm Workspaces
nodes.rationale: pnpm workspaces without Turborepo keep the monorepo small. packages/tooling from the Phase 0 layout was dropped; shared config lives in the root tsconfig.base.json and eslint.config.mjs.

nodes.label: Tenant Isolation
nodes.rationale: Isolation is app-level scoping plus PostgreSQL row level security with SET LOCAL per transaction, fail-closed, and composite foreign keys. Frontend filtering is not a security boundary.

nodes.label: Railway Hosting
nodes.rationale: Railway is the V1 host only after a backup restore has been verified. Kubernetes and microservices are avoided unless a concrete requirement appears.

nodes.label: No Customer PII in V1
nodes.rationale: Customer personal data is not stored in V1, which keeps privacy webhooks as acknowledgements and avoids a data-use change.

nodes.label: Table Naming Prefixes
nodes.rationale: Tables are lowercase snake_case with prefixes m_, s_, t_, f_, o_, and a_ so a name records what the data is and who creates it. Prefixes are not carried into TypeScript names.

nodes.label: @pi/seed
nodes.rationale: Development-only seeder. It never ships with the product. The same seed is deterministic, and sourceIdentifier pi-seed plus the pi-seed tag make re-runs idempotent.

nodes.label: Seed Manifest
nodes.rationale: packages/seed/out/manifest.json stores Shopify-reported totals per order and month. It is the ground truth for reconciling sync and the profit engine.

nodes.label: Partner Development Guard
nodes.rationale: The seeder refuses to run unless the store reports plan.partnerDevelopment and NODE_ENV is not production, so write traffic cannot hit a live store.

nodes.label: processedAt as Analytics Date
nodes.rationale: orderCreate honours a past processedAt, but createdAt is always the import time. Analytics must use processed_at. Orders created now are readable without read_all_orders, so this data does not exercise the 60-day created_at limit.

nodes.label: Date Refunds from refund.processedAt
nodes.rationale: refundCreate honours a past processedAt on the refund, but the REFUND transaction keeps today's timestamp. Refunds must be dated from refund.processedAt, never from the transaction.

nodes.label: Read-Only Shopify Scopes
nodes.rationale: The released app asks for read access only. Write scopes are a temporary seed exception. tests/app-config.test.ts fails while any write scope remains in shopify.app.toml.

nodes.label: app-config.test.ts
nodes.rationale: Fails the build if shopify.app.toml still contains write scopes, so the seed-time privilege increase cannot ship.

nodes.label: summarizePeriod
nodes.rationale: One function in packages/profit-engine/src/period.ts turns a period's stored sums into every Overview, Profit, Marketing, Products, profit-and-loss, CSV, PDF, and scheduled-email figure. Nothing else adds up revenue, costs, advertising, or expenses.

nodes.label: Revenue
nodes.rationale: Revenue is net sales plus shipping charged net of refunds. Net sales are gross sales minus discounts minus product refunds. Tax is never revenue.

nodes.label: Contribution Profit
nodes.rationale: Contribution before advertising is revenue minus product cost, payment fees, and shipping cost. Advertising is subtracted only when advertising data exists; otherwise profit excludes advertising and says so. Platform-reported sales stay apart from Shopify revenue and spend is not allocated to products or orders.

nodes.label: Estimated Net Profit
nodes.rationale: Estimated net profit is contribution profit minus operating expenses only when expenses are set up. Otherwise the figure is not available, so a partial contribution is not labelled as accounting-grade net profit.

nodes.label: Data Status
nodes.rationale: Zero is not missing. An amount is never inferred. Statuses are confirmed (including a confirmed zero), estimated, missing, not_configured, and not_applicable. The weakest entry wins. Exports write words such as Missing instead of 0 so a spreadsheet cannot read a gap as zero.

nodes.label: Cash View Refunds
nodes.rationale: A refund counts on its processed date in the shop time zone, not the order date and not the settlement date. Past months stay unchanged. Discounts are not taken off twice. Payment fees are not returned because the Admin API does not expose a reversed fee. Restocked goods bring cost back on the refund date.

nodes.label: Frozen Ledger Unit Cost
nodes.rationale: Each line's cost is frozen in the ledger. Resolution order is the earlier calculation, then the latest merchant cost on or before the order date, then Shopify's current unit cost as Estimated, otherwise Missing never zero. Changing a cost today does not rewrite earlier orders. Only an explicit audited recalculate does; fill gaps prices only lines that were missing.

nodes.label: Decimal Money
nodes.rationale: Money uses decimal.js in code and numeric(19,4) in the database. Each ledger entry is rounded once, half away from zero, to the currency minor unit. Floating point is never used for money.

nodes.label: D1 Cash View
nodes.rationale: A refund reduces profit in the period it was issued, using refund.processed_at. Past periods never change. The accrual alternative was rejected because it would rewrite the order's period when a refund arrives. The REFUND transaction timestamp is never used.

nodes.label: D2 Counted Orders
nodes.rationale: Only PAID, PARTIALLY_REFUNDED, and REFUNDED count, because money was collected. Pending, authorized, partially paid, voided, expired, cancelled-unpaid, and test orders are awaiting payment. Counting every non-cancelled order like Shopify analytics would overstate profit.

nodes.label: D3 Shopify Cost Is Estimated
nodes.rationale: Shopify stores only the current unit cost, so applying it to an old order may be wrong. A merchant cost with an effective date is Actual. Shopify's current cost on a past order is Estimated. No cost is Missing. Treating Shopify's cost as Actual was rejected because it misleads after cost changes.

nodes.label: D4 Missing Data Is Never Zero
nodes.rationale: No fee rule, shipping rule, or unit cost leaves the component Missing and the profit partial. Defaulting silently to zero was rejected because profit would look better than it is. A missing cost must not be called a confirmed loss.
nodes.norm_label: d4 missing data is never zero

nodes.label: D5 Profit Confidence
nodes.rationale: High, Medium, and Low measure data completeness, not statistical probability. Weights are 60 percent product cost, 20 percent fees, and 20 percent shipping. High is at least 0.90 and Medium at least 0.60. A numeric percentage was rejected as false precision.

nodes.label: D6 Gift Cards
nodes.rationale: Gift cards are a liability until redeemed, so gift-card product lines are excluded from sales and shown separately rather than treated as normal revenue.

nodes.label: D7 USD to AED Peg
nodes.rationale: The AED peg is 3.6725 per USD and is marked Actual. Every other pair needs a daily rate on the entry date, marked Estimated. A missing rate makes the converted value Missing, never 1.0. Original amount and currency are never overwritten.

nodes.label: D8 Variant Cost Granularity
nodes.rationale: Product cost is stored per variant with an effective date and applies until the next entry. Per-product storage was rejected because variants can be priced differently.

nodes.label: Business Date processed_at
nodes.rationale: The business date is processed_at in the shop time zone. Daily and monthly totals sum ledger entries by that date. The rate used for conversion is the rate on the entry date, not today's rate.

nodes.label: COGS Resolution
nodes.rationale: Cost per unit is the latest merchant cost with effective_from on or before the business date. Otherwise Shopify's current unit cost is Estimated. Otherwise the line is Missing. Lines without a cost contribute 0 to COGS and still count in the missing share. A change does not silently rewrite historical profit.

nodes.label: f_product_cost
nodes.rationale: Append-only per-variant cost history with who, when, and why. Entries can be revoked, not edited. Rows are keyed by Shopify variant id so a deleted variant keeps its merchant cost. Historical cost changes are seeded here, not in Shopify.

nodes.label: s_payment_fee_rule
nodes.rationale: Actual fee is what Shopify Payments reports. Otherwise the merchant rule is percentage plus fixed amount, rounded, and marked Estimated. If neither exists the fee is Missing. Refunds do not reduce a fixed fee.

nodes.label: s_shipping_cost_rule
nodes.rationale: Shopify does not report carrier cost, so shipping cost comes from an effective-dated merchant rule. Free-shipping orders can still cost money to ship. No rule is Missing. An explicit 0 is Actual-by-declaration. Nothing to ship is not applicable.

nodes.label: Component Status Model
nodes.rationale: Every ledger component is Actual, Estimated, Missing, or Not applicable. Aggregates carry the weakest status of their parts. The UI always shows which part is which so an estimate is not presented as an exact fact.

nodes.label: Profit Ledger
nodes.rationale: One entry per component per event stores order id, event date, signed shop-currency amount, status, source, inputs, and engine_version. Every dashboard number can be listed back to entries. Results are recomputed idempotently per order after a sync, webhook, or cost or rule change.

nodes.label: Golden Tests
nodes.rationale: Section 14 examples come from the seeded dev store, not invented numbers. The engine must reproduce them exactly. pnpm profit:verify re-checks them against the live dev store.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL Custom Dump
nodes.rationale: The dump covers business data, settings, the audit log, and the job queue. Shopify can re-supply orders, but costs, rules, expenses, ad spend, and the audit log exist only here, which is why backups matter. A SHA-256 manifest and row-count snapshot make an unreadable file fail the run. Suggested retention is 14 daily backups.

nodes.label: backup:verify
nodes.rationale: A backup that has never been restored is a hope. Verify checks the checksum, restores into a temporary database, compares tables, row counts, forced row level security, policies, and migrations, then always drops the temporary database.

nodes.label: Forward-Only Migrations
nodes.rationale: Migrations are never edited after release and have no down script. Recovery from a bad migration is to restore the backup taken just before it, fix the migration, and run it again. A drop or rewrite must carry an explicit destructive approval or a test fails. Take a backup immediately before every production migration.

nodes.label: assertProductionConfig
nodes.rationale: Production start-up refuses unsafe settings and lists them without printing secret values: NODE_ENV, https APP_URL, database TLS, a fresh TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY, the production Shopify secret, and billing test mode off.

nodes.label: read_all_orders Before Launch
nodes.rationale: Orders older than 60 days need read_all_orders. The app keeps 90 days, so launch requires that approval or the history window must be lowered to 60 days.

nodes.label: TLS Reverse Proxy
nodes.rationale: TLS terminates at the reverse proxy. The web app forwards /api/v1 to the API on a private address. API and web send HSTS. The worker port and API port are not exposed directly.

nodes.label: Incident Severity
nodes.rationale: Level 1 is data exposure or wrong money and is acted on at once. A suspected cross-shop leak stops the API before investigation, because a stopped app is better than a leaking one. Level 1 that touched merchant data requires prompt notice to Shopify Partner support and the merchants.

nodes.label: Secret Rotation
nodes.rationale: The Shopify API secret is rotated in one step on API and worker because webhook signature checks use it. A new TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY is added under a new key id so existing tokens keep working until merchants sign in again. After any rotation, pnpm audit:secrets must show the old value nowhere.

nodes.label: ops.monitor
nodes.rationale: The worker runs ops.monitor every 15 minutes and writes one warning per problem as a structured JSON log line with a stable event name such as sync_stale, webhook_backlog, or delivery_failed. Each stale shop is also told once a day.

nodes.label: Health Endpoints
nodes.rationale: Worker GET /status returns problem counts and names no shop, order, or customer. GET /health is liveness. pnpm health checks web, API, and worker. The status port stays on the private network.

nodes.label: In-Memory Rate Limit
nodes.rationale: Rate-limit counters live in each API process. With more than one process the limit applies per process, so the counter must move to the database or a cache before scaling out.

nodes.label: No Stored Customer Personal Data
nodes.rationale: Customer names, emails, addresses, and phone numbers are never requested or stored. A test asserts no table has such a column. Report recipient emails and an optional feedback reply address are merchant-typed, not customer records. Storing customer personal data would require updating this policy and the data-use declaration.

nodes.label: purgeShopData
nodes.rationale: One transaction deletes every row of the shop, the shop, and the tenant when no other shop remains. Row level security limits the delete to that tenant. A test fills every table with a shop id and fails if a new table is not covered.

nodes.label: 30-Day Uninstall Grace
nodes.rationale: app/uninstalled removes the token at once and schedules a purge in 30 days, skipped if the merchant reinstalled. shop/redact deletes immediately and overrides the grace period. Shopify's required deletion timelines override the 30-day preference.

nodes.label: Plan Downgrade Does Not Delete
nodes.rationale: A smaller plan limits what can be viewed, prepared, scheduled, and connected. Nothing is deleted. Scheduled emails over the new limit are paused, not removed. Cancelling a subscription is a change of plan to Free.

nodes.label: Report File Retention
nodes.rationale: CSV and PDF report files are kept 7 days and removed by the nightly cleanup. Orders stay for the 90-day history window. A plan limits how much history can be viewed, never what is kept.

nodes.label: SessionGuard
nodes.rationale: Every controller except health and the signed webhook endpoint is behind SessionGuard. The tenant comes from the signed App Bridge token, never from the request. Forged shop or tenant ids are ignored.

nodes.label: Forced Row Level Security
nodes.rationale: Every table with tenant_id has forced row level security and one policy using app_current_tenant(). The application role is not a superuser, cannot bypass RLS, owns no tables, and cannot create objects. Cross-tenant policies are an allow-list. A new table without RLS fails the security integration test.

nodes.label: AES-256-GCM Token Encryption
nodes.rationale: Shopify access tokens are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM and a key id for rotation, and decrypted only in memory. Logs strip secrets by pattern and field name. Requests are logged by route pattern, never by path, query, body, or headers.

nodes.label: Rotate Shopify API Secret
nodes.rationale: The review found a real-looking Shopify secret in .env.example. It was removed, but anyone who saw the file still has it, so a new secret must be created in the Dev Dashboard and stored only in .env.

nodes.label: Idempotent Jobs
nodes.rationale: pg-boss retries a throwing job with backoff and one failure does not stop others. Every job is safe to run twice: syncs and recalculation replace rather than append, so retries cannot double-count money.

nodes.label: withTenant Job Context
nodes.rationale: Every job payload carries tenantId and shopId and runs inside withTenant. Cross-shop jobs use a read-only system context, then switch to the tenant for every write. Job payloads carry ids only.

nodes.label: Local PostgreSQL 17
nodes.rationale: Development credentials only and must never be reused in production. The compose service runs postgres:17, database profit_intelligence, published on host port 5433.

nodes.label: Profit Intelligence Product Vision
nodes.rationale: The core promise is connect Shopify, calculate real profit, detect profit leakage, explain the cause, and recommend an action. The differentiator is profit transparency, not another generic analytics dashboard. V1 stays focused before an AI CFO or forecasting.

nodes.label: Product Design Principles
nodes.rationale: Financial transparency beats unexplained numbers. Actual, estimated, and missing data must always be distinguishable. Every important profit figure must be explainable. Build a reliable core before AI, isolate tenants from the start, and keep the stack suitable for a solo developer.

nodes.label: Phase Gate
nodes.rationale: Implement one phase at a time and stop for approval. Do not claim a command or test succeeded unless it was executed. Keep financial rules in a testable domain layer. Database constraints add integrity and do not replace application authorization.

nodes.label: Financial Calculation Contract
nodes.rationale: Accounting semantics must be a written reviewed specification, not developer or model assumptions. The starting model is gross sales minus discounts and refunds equals net sales, then minus COGS, shipping cost, payment fees, and advertising equals contribution profit, then minus operating expenses equals estimated net profit. Never silently invent unavailable values. Advertising-attributed revenue is not Shopify revenue.

nodes.label: Profit Leakage Detection
nodes.rationale: The first detector is deterministic rules, not an AI dependency. It must not label a condition as a confirmed loss when the underlying cost data is incomplete. Each issue needs evidence, a defensible impact, data limitations, and a next action.

nodes.label: Approved Phase 0 Decisions
nodes.rationale: Section 31 records the approved stack: Next.js plus a separate API, NestJS on Fastify, Drizzle, pg-boss with no Redis, pnpm workspaces, RLS with SET LOCAL, Railway gated on a verified restore, no customer PII, 90-day history, and High/Medium/Low profit confidence. Refund timing was to be re-confirmed in the written calculation spec.

nodes.label: Database Naming Convention
nodes.rationale: Section 32 defines singular snake_case tables, prefixes m_ s_ t_ f_ o_ a_, tenant_id as the first business column, and constraint names pk_ fk_ uq_ ix_. Classification follows what the data is and who creates it.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL Database profit_intelligence
nodes.rationale: Section 0.1 names database profit_intelligence. The development superuser is replaced by a least-privilege app_user. The password lives only in the git-ignored .env. Node uses a postgresql:// URL, not a Python driver prefix.
